chapter_title: CHAPTER 18 SEARCHing foR CASE LAw
text: Relevant cases can then be found in a number of ways depending on the features of the research tool being used and the researcher’s own knowledge of the subject.
text_raw:
Relevant cases can then be found in a number 
of ways depending on the features of the research tool being used and the researcher’s 
own knowledge of the subject.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 18 SEARCHing foR CASE LAw
text: In some databases, cases are arranged under broad subject headings.
text_raw:
In some databases, cases are arranged under broad subject 
headings.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 18 SEARCHing foR CASE LAw
text: It is possible to browse for cases under these subject headings then drill down further into narrower subheadings.
text_raw:
It is possible to browse for cases under these subject headings then drill down 
further into narrower subheadings.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 18 SEARCHing foR CASE LAw
text: Legal databases also allow the researcher to find cases relevant to the legal issue and facts of the problem by entering key words and phrases into different search fields.
text_raw:
Legal databases also allow the researcher to find cases 
relevant to the legal issue and facts of the problem by entering key words and phrases into 
different search fields.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 18 SEARCHing foR CASE LAw
text: In a hierarchical system like the common law the researcher will generally focus on finding binding cases or cases of high authority, usually from superior courts (see discussion of hierarchy of courts starting at 8.17ff).
text_raw:
In a hierarchical system like the common law the researcher will generally focus on 
finding binding cases or cases of high authority, usually from superior courts (see discussion 
of hierarchy of courts starting at 8.17ff).

chapter_title: CHAPTER 18 SEARCHing foR CASE LAw
text: However, depending on the outcome of the early stages of the search, the researcher may need to rely on cases of persuasive authority from another jurisdiction or from decisions of courts lower in the same hierarchy. finDing CASE CiTATionS Sometimes only the name of a case will be given and the researcher will need to find the complete citation in order to locate it.
text_raw:
However, depending on the outcome of the 
early stages of the search, the researcher may need to rely on cases of persuasive authority 
from another jurisdiction or from decisions of courts lower in the same hierarchy.
finDing CASE CiTATionS
Sometimes only the name of a case will be given and the researcher will need to find the 
complete citation in order to locate it.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 18 SEARCHing foR CASE LAw
text: When citing a case in any form of legal writing, a researcher must always provide a complete citation.
text_raw:
When citing a case in any form of legal writing, 
a researcher must always provide a complete citation.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 18 SEARCHing foR CASE LAw
text: This should preferably be from an authorised series of law reports when available, or the medium neutral citation (see 21.15–21.16).
text_raw:
This should preferably be from an 
authorised series of law reports when available, or the medium neutral citation 
(see 21.15–21.16).

chapter_title: CHAPTER 18 SEARCHing foR CASE LAw
text: The need to find alternative citations may also arise because one or more of the citations may refer to a series of law reports that is unavailable.
text_raw:

text: Finding judicial consideration of cases As discussed at 18.16 and 18.17, CaseBase (via Lexis Advance) and FirstPoint (via Westlaw AU) are very important databases for case law research.
text_raw:
Finding judicial consideration of cases
As discussed at 18.16 and 18.17, CaseBase (via Lexis Advance) and FirstPoint (via Westlaw AU) 
are very important databases for case law research.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 18 SEARCHing foR CASE LAw
text: One of the key features of both is the ability to find detailed information about the extent to which cases have received subsequent judicial consideration (sometimes referred to as the ‘subsequent history’ of the case).
text_raw:
One of the key features of both is 
the ability to find detailed information about the extent to which cases have received 
subsequent judicial consideration (sometimes referred to as the ‘subsequent history’ of 
the case).

chapter_title: CHAPTER 18 SEARCHing foR CASE LAw
text: CaseBase signals indicate the kind of treatment a case has received: positive (green plus sign), negative (red cross) or cautionary (orange exclamation mark). ‘CaseBase Signal Help’ provides a full explanation of each signal.
text_raw:
CaseBase signals indicate the kind of treatment a case has received: positive 
(green plus sign), negative (red cross) or cautionary (orange exclamation mark). ‘CaseBase 
Signal Help’ provides a full explanation of each signal.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 18 SEARCHing foR CASE LAw
text: The researcher can then look at a complete list (or a graph providing an overview) of ‘Cases referring to this case’, all of which contain a colour-coded annotation stating how the corresponding case was treated (such as ‘applied’ in green or ‘overruled’ in red).

CHAPTER 19 SEARCHing foR LEgiSLATion
text: Introduction Since it is the predominant source of law, few legal problems can be resolved without reference to legislation.
text_raw:
Introduction
Since it is the predominant source of law, few legal problems can be resolved without 
reference to legislation.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 19 SEARCHing foR LEgiSLATion
text: The ability to find legislation is therefore critical, not only for researchers but also citizens, who are assumed to know the law.
text_raw:
The ability to find legislation is therefore critical, not only for 
researchers but also citizens, who are assumed to know the law.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 19 SEARCHing foR LEgiSLATion
text: This assumption is expressed in the well-known adage ‘ignorance of the law is no excuse’, affirmed by the High Court in Ostrowski v Palmer.2 In this case the conviction of a professional fisherman for fishing for rock lobsters in a prohibited area was unanimously upheld, even though his decision to fish there was based on misleading information provided by the Western Australia fisheries department.
text_raw:
This assumption is 
expressed in the well-known adage ‘ignorance of the law is no excuse’, affirmed by the 
High Court in Ostrowski v Palmer.2 In this case the conviction of a professional fisherman 
for fishing for rock lobsters in a prohibited area was unanimously upheld, even though 
his decision to fish there was based on misleading information provided by the Western 
Australia fisheries department.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 19 SEARCHing foR LEgiSLATion
text: It is important to not only be able to find legislation but also to be confident that you have found the correct version of the law.
text_raw:
It is important to not only be able to find legislation but also to be confident that 
you have found the correct version of the law.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 19 SEARCHing foR LEgiSLATion
text: This will usually involve identifying the law currently in force but sometimes involves identifying how the law stood at a particular point in the past, which requires a search for a historical version of legislation.
text_raw:
This will usually involve identifying the law 
currently in force but sometimes involves identifying how the law stood at a particular 
point in the past, which requires a search for a historical version of legislation.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 19 SEARCHing foR LEgiSLATion
text: The volume of new Acts and delegated legislation made each year, as well as the myriad amendments to existing legislation, can make searching for the relevant law time-consuming, even with the assistance of online sources.
text_raw:
The volume 
of new Acts and delegated legislation made each year, as well as the myriad amendments 
to existing legislation, can make searching for the relevant law time-consuming, even 
with the assistance of online sources.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 19 SEARCHing foR LEgiSLATion
text: Being able to use effective methods for finding legislative material not only saves time but also means the researcher can be confident of having correctly identified the relevant law.
text_raw:
Being able to use effective methods for finding 
legislative material not only saves time but also means the researcher can be confident of 
having correctly identified the relevant law.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 19 SEARCHing foR LEgiSLATion
text: This chapter offers strategies and skills to perform the range of tasks needed to research legislation effectively.
text_raw:
This chapter offers strategies and skills to perform the range of tasks needed to 
research legislation effectively.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 19 SEARCHing foR LEgiSLATion
text: These tasks include: • finding known Acts and delegated legislation, either the most current versions or other versions; • tracking the history of a piece legislation, including its date of commencement and amendments that have been made to it over time; • finding legislation on a topic; • finding cases and commentary referring to legislation; and • finding extrinsic materials related to an Act to help understand its meaning or purpose.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 19 SEARCHing foR LEgiSLATion
text: These tasks are discussed in detail in the rest of the chapter.
text_raw: These tasks are discussed in detail in the rest of the chapter.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 19 SEARCHing foR LEgiSLATion
text: At the end of the chapter there is an exercise that can be used to test your ability to find information about Commonwealth legislative materials.
text_raw:
At the end of the chapter 
there is an exercise that can be used to test your ability to find information about 
Commonwealth legislative materials.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 19 SEARCHing foR LEgiSLATion
text: Acts and delegated legislation Before moving to a detailed discussion of the tasks associated with researching Acts and delegated legislation it is worth briefly recapping some key terminology.
text_raw:
Acts and delegated legislation
Before moving to a detailed discussion of the tasks associated with researching Acts and 
delegated legislation it is worth briefly recapping some key terminology.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 19 SEARCHing foR LEgiSLATion
text: The terms ‘Act’ and ‘statute’ have exactly the same meaning: they are enactments of Parliament.
text_raw:
The terms ‘Act’ 
and ‘statute’ have exactly the same meaning: they are enactments of Parliament.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 19 SEARCHing foR LEgiSLATion
text: As discussed at 9.2–9.4, ‘legislation’ is a term used to describe Acts or statutes, as well as delegated legislation (also referred to as ‘subordinate legislation’ or ‘legislative instruments’), which refers to those laws made by persons or bodies to whom Parliament has delegated law- making authority.
text_raw:
As discussed 
at 9.2–9.4, ‘legislation’ is a term used to describe Acts or statutes, as well as delegated 
legislation (also referred to as ‘subordinate legislation’ or ‘legislative instruments’), which 
refers to those laws made by persons or bodies to whom Parliament has delegated law-
making authority.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 19 SEARCHing foR LEgiSLATion
text: Examples include regulations, statutory rules, ordinances and by-laws.
text_raw: Examples include regulations, statutory rules, ordinances and by-laws.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 19 SEARCHing foR LEgiSLATion
text: Formerly, legislation was found in print copy annual volumes.
text_raw: Formerly, legislation was found in print copy annual volumes.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 19 SEARCHing foR LEgiSLATion
text: As legislation is often amended (sometimes very frequently), finding the version in force at a particular time was often difficult.
text_raw:
As legislation is often 
amended (sometimes very frequently), finding the version in force at a particular time 
was often difficult.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 19 SEARCHing foR LEgiSLATion
text: This issue was sometimes solved by a consolidation (see 9.71) or a reprint (see 9.72) incorporating the changes.
text_raw:
This issue was sometimes solved by a consolidation (see 9.71) or a 
reprint (see 9.72) incorporating the changes.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 19 SEARCHing foR LEgiSLATion
text: But these would not always provide the researcher with the latest version of the Act, and it is usually (but not always) current law that students and lawyers are expected to apply.
text_raw:
But these would not always provide the 
researcher with the latest version of the Act, and it is usually (but not always) current 
law that students and lawyers are expected to apply.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 19 SEARCHing foR LEgiSLATion
text: Thankfully, online resources have largely made such difficulties a thing of the past, as well as making many of the other tasks associated with researching legislation significantly easier and less time-consuming than was previously the case.
text_raw:
Thankfully, online resources have 
largely made such difficulties a thing of the past, as well as making many of the other tasks 
associated with researching legislation significantly easier and less time-consuming than 
was previously the case.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 19 SEARCHing foR LEgiSLATion
text: Finding known Acts and delegated legislation The first step towards finding an Act is to discover its short title, which is the name by which it is commonly known and cited.
text_raw:
Finding known Acts and delegated legislation
The first step towards finding an Act is to discover its short title, which is the name by 
which it is commonly known and cited.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 19 SEARCHing foR LEgiSLATion
text: Delegated (or subordinate) legislation often has a title that is a variant of the title of the principal Act under which it operates.
text_raw:
Delegated (or subordinate) legislation often has a 
title that is a variant of the title of the principal Act under which it operates.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 19 SEARCHing foR LEgiSLATion
text: In cases where the title of an Act has no apparent connection with the title of the delegated legislation, finding subordinate legislation can be more difficult.
text_raw:
In cases where 
the title of an Act has no apparent connection with the title of the delegated legislation, 
finding subordinate legislation can be more difficult.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 19 SEARCHing foR LEgiSLATion
text: However, many (but not all) online research tools provide a link to the delegated legislation enabled by a particular Act.
text_raw:
However, many (but not all) online 
research tools provide a link to the delegated legislation enabled by a particular Act.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 19 SEARCHing foR LEgiSLATion
text: In any event, law students will often already know the names of the Acts and delegated legislation they need to find because they will be identified in their course outline or textbooks.
text_raw:
In any 
event, law students will often already know the names of the Acts and delegated legislation 
they need to find because they will be identified in their course outline or textbooks.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 19 SEARCHing foR LEgiSLATion
text: Researchers have a wide range of choices for accessing the full text of legislation online.
text_raw:
Researchers have a wide range of choices for accessing the full text of legislation 
online.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 19 SEARCHing foR LEgiSLATion
text: These include government websites where legislation can be accessed for a particular jurisdiction.
text_raw:
These include government websites where legislation can be accessed for a 
particular jurisdiction.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 19 SEARCHing foR LEgiSLATion
text: There are also websites and subscription databases providing access to legislation for all Australian jurisdictions.
text_raw:
There are also websites and subscription databases providing access 
to legislation for all Australian jurisdictions.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 19 SEARCHing foR LEgiSLATion
text: Most websites and databases provide access to current (also known as ‘consolidated’ or ‘in force’) versions of Acts and delegated legislation as well as the original (known as ‘numbered’ or ‘as made’) versions.
text_raw:
Most websites and databases provide access 
to current (also known as ‘consolidated’ or ‘in force’) versions of Acts and delegated 
legislation as well as the original (known as ‘numbered’ or ‘as made’) versions.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 19 SEARCHing foR LEgiSLATion
text: Some also provide access to repealed legislation (legislation no longer in force) and ‘point in time’ legislation, where a version of an Act or piece of delegated legislation can be viewed as it stood at a particular date or time.
text_raw:
Some also 
provide access to repealed legislation (legislation no longer in force) and ‘point in time’ 
legislation, where a version of an Act or piece of delegated legislation can be viewed as it 
stood at a particular date or time.

CHAPTER 19 SEARCHing foR LEgiSLATion
text: Tracking the history of Acts and delegated legislation It is very important, in a variety of contexts, for researchers to be able to successfully track the history of legislative materials.
text_raw:
Tracking the history of Acts and delegated 
legislation
It is very important, in a variety of contexts, for researchers to be able to successfully 
track the history of legislative materials.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 19 SEARCHing foR LEgiSLATion
text: For example, as mentioned at 9.17ff, the date of commencement of legislation (that is, the date it comes into force and starts operating as law) may be pivotal to the guilt or innocence of a person, to their entitlement to a pension, or their eligibility for a licence.
text_raw:
For example, as mentioned at 9.17ff, the date of 
commencement of legislation (that is, the date it comes into force and starts operating as law) 
may be pivotal to the guilt or innocence of a person, to their entitlement to a pension, or 
their eligibility for a licence.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 19 SEARCHing foR LEgiSLATion
text: As mentioned at 9.34ff, legislation, or sections of legislation, may also be subject to frequent change via amendments, or even repealed.
text_raw:
As mentioned at 9.34ff, legislation, or sections of legislation, 
may also be subject to frequent change via amendments, or even repealed.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 19 SEARCHing foR LEgiSLATion
text: It is therefore vital that a lawyer is aware of the amendment history of an Act or piece of delegated legislation, and does not mistakenly rely on a provision that is not applicable to their client.
text_raw:
It is therefore 
vital that a lawyer is aware of the amendment history of an Act or piece of delegated 
legislation, and does not mistakenly rely on a provision that is not applicable to their 
client.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 19 SEARCHing foR LEgiSLATion
text: For example, if a client’s matter took place on 1 June 2018, the relevant version of an Act may be the one that was in operation at that time.
text_raw:
For example, if a client’s matter took place on 1 June 2018, the relevant version of 
an Act may be the one that was in operation at that time.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 19 SEARCHing foR LEgiSLATion
text: Subsequent amendments to that Act made after 1 June 2018 may not be applicable.
text_raw:
Subsequent amendments to that 
Act made after 1 June 2018 may not be applicable.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 19 SEARCHing foR LEgiSLATion
text: The date of commencement and amendment history of legislation can be found in the endnotes (note that the date of commencement is sometimes also specified in an early provision of an Act or piece of delegated legislation).
text_raw:
The date of commencement and amendment history of legislation can be found in 
the endnotes (note that the date of commencement is sometimes also specified in an early 
provision of an Act or piece of delegated legislation).

chapter_title: CHAPTER 19 SEARCHing foR LEgiSLATion
text: The term ‘Historical Notes’ is used instead of ‘Endnotes’ in older legislation and in some jurisdictions, such as New South Wales.
text_raw:
The term ‘Historical Notes’ is used 
instead of ‘Endnotes’ in older legislation and in some jurisdictions, such as New South 
Wales.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 19 SEARCHing foR LEgiSLATion
text: A step-by-step example of interpreting the information in the endnotes in a Commonwealth Act, using the Federal Register of Legislation, follows at 19.19.
text_raw:
A step-by-step example of interpreting the information in the endnotes in a 
Commonwealth Act, using the Federal Register of Legislation, follows at 19.19.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 19 SEARCHing foR LEgiSLATion
text: T wo tables can generally be found in the endnotes and these list legislation that has changed the Act and the sections that have been changed.
text_raw:
T wo tables can generally be found in the endnotes and these list legislation that 
has changed the Act and the sections that have been changed.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 19 SEARCHing foR LEgiSLATion
text: The first table is called ‘Legislation History’ (or in some jurisdictions the ‘Table of Amending Instruments’).
text_raw:
The first table is called 
‘Legislation History’ (or in some jurisdictions the ‘Table of Amending Instruments’).

chapter_title: CHAPTER 19 SEARCHing foR LEgiSLATion
text: At the top of this table the researcher will find the date of commencement.
text_raw: At the top of this table the researcher will find the date of commencement.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 19 SEARCHing foR LEgiSLATion
text: This table will also contain a chronological list of amending legislation responsible for altering the operation of the Act or piece of delegated legislation.
text_raw:
This table 
will also contain a chronological list of amending legislation responsible for altering the 
operation of the Act or piece of delegated legislation.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 19 SEARCHing foR LEgiSLATion
text: The second table in the endnotes is called ‘Amendment History’ (or in some jurisdictions the ‘Table of Amendments’).
text_raw:
The second table in the endnotes 
is called ‘Amendment History’ (or in some jurisdictions the ‘Table of Amendments’).

chapter_title: CHAPTER 19 SEARCHing foR LEgiSLATion
text: This table provides a list of changes to an Act or piece of delegated legislation provision by provision.
text_raw:
This table provides a list of changes to an Act or piece of delegated legislation provision 
by provision.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 19 SEARCHing foR LEgiSLATion
text: While the amendment history of legislation in the endnotes is vital for all of the reasons stated above, researchers may also want to be aware of any proposed amendments to legislation that may impact on their clients.
text_raw:
While the amendment history of legislation in the endnotes is vital for all of the 
reasons stated above, researchers may also want to be aware of any proposed amendments to 
legislation that may impact on their clients.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 19 SEARCHing foR LEgiSLATion
text: Finding legislation by topic As stated at 19.5, law students are often provided with a list of the most important Acts and delegated legislation for the subjects in which they are enrolled.
text_raw:
Finding legislation by topic
As stated at 19.5, law students are often provided with a list of the most important Acts 
and delegated legislation for the subjects in which they are enrolled.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 19 SEARCHing foR LEgiSLATion
text: However, when undertaking research assignments (and, of course, in legal practice) it will be necessary to locate legislation on a particular topic.
text_raw:
However, when 
undertaking research assignments (and, of course, in legal practice) it will be necessary 
to locate legislation on a particular topic.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 19 SEARCHing foR LEgiSLATion
text: It was mentioned in the earlier legal research chapters that when looking for information on a legal topic or principle, it is often wise to consult secondary sources of law before delving into the detail of primary materials.
text_raw:
It was mentioned in the earlier legal research 
chapters that when looking for information on a legal topic or principle, it is often wise 
to consult secondary sources of law before delving into the detail of primary materials.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 19 SEARCHing foR LEgiSLATion
text: Legislation on a topic can be located using secondary sources of law such as textbooks, legal encyclopedias and journal articles (see Chapter 17 for more information on these sources).
text_raw:
Legislation on a topic can be located using secondary sources of law such as textbooks, 
legal encyclopedias and journal articles (see Chapter 17 for more information on these 
sources).

chapter_title: CHAPTER 19 SEARCHing foR LEgiSLATion
text: All of the specialist legislation websites and databases referred to at 19.8ff have advanced searching functions (albeit of varying levels of sophistication) to allow the researcher to locate legislation by topic.

advanced searching functions (albeit of varying levels of sophistication) to allow the

text: 534 LAYING DOWN THE LAW However, it is sometimes difficult to obtain meaningful results using the search feature of databases to find legislation by topic, particularly when searching for words across the full text of Acts and delegated legislation.
text_raw:
534
LAYING DOWN THE LAW
However, it is sometimes difficult to obtain meaningful results using the search 
feature of databases to find legislation by topic, particularly when searching for words 
across the full text of Acts and delegated legislation.

use an online case citator.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 19 SEARCHing foR LEgiSLATion
CHAPTER 19 SEARCHing foR LEgiSLATion
text: Finding commentary about legislation Researchers interested in obtaining an overview of relevant legislation on a topic, or an understanding of how a particular piece of legislation fits into its broader legal context, will benefit from finding commentary about legislation.
text_raw:
Finding commentary about legislation
Researchers interested in obtaining an overview of relevant legislation on a topic, 
or an understanding of how a particular piece of legislation fits into its broader legal 
context, will benefit from finding commentary about legislation.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 19 SEARCHing foR LEgiSLATion
text: Commentary can be found in the secondary sources of law discussed in Chapter 17, including textbooks, legal encyclopedias, law reform commission publications, parliamentary reports and journal articles.
text_raw:
Commentary can be 
found in the secondary sources of law discussed in Chapter 17, including textbooks, 
legal encyclopedias, law reform commission publications, parliamentary reports and 
journal articles.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 19 SEARCHing foR LEgiSLATion
text: Another important source is the commentary sections of the three major online legal publisher platforms in Australia:
text_raw:
Another important source is the commentary sections of the three 
major online legal publisher platforms in Australia:

chapter_title: CHAPTER 19 SEARCHing foR LEgiSLATion
text: CCH IntelliConnect, Lexis Advance and Westlaw AU.
text_raw:
CCH IntelliConnect, Lexis Advance 
and Westlaw AU.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 19 SEARCHing foR LEgiSLATion
text: While some commentary is written in a descriptive, objective style, journal articles are more likely to critique the law, alerting researchers to potential areas of uncertainty and controversy in legislation.
text_raw:
While some commentary is written in a descriptive, objective style, journal articles 
are more likely to critique the law, alerting researchers to potential areas of uncertainty 
and controversy in legislation.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 19 SEARCHing foR LEgiSLATion
text: A good place to find references to Australian journal articles discussing legislation is the collection of legal databases available on the subscription- based Informit online platform.
text_raw:
A good place to find references to Australian journal articles 
discussing legislation is the collection of legal databases available on the subscription-
based Informit online platform.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 19 SEARCHing foR LEgiSLATion
text: These include AGIS Plus Text, a comprehensive index to articles from over 200 Australian, New Zealand and Asia Pacific journals, and CINCH – Australian Criminology Database.
text_raw:
These include AGIS Plus Text, a comprehensive index to 
articles from over 200 Australian, New Zealand and Asia Pacific journals, and CINCH – 
Australian Criminology Database.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 19 SEARCHing foR LEgiSLATion
text: When performing an Advanced Search in AGIS Plus Text, the researcher is able to select ‘Legislation’ from the ‘Any Field’ drop-down menu, then enter the legislation name as a search term to find journal articles referring to that piece of legislation.
text_raw:
When performing an Advanced Search in AGIS Plus Text, 
the researcher is able to select ‘Legislation’ from the ‘Any Field’ drop-down menu, then 
enter the legislation name as a search term to find journal articles referring to that piece 
of legislation.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 19 SEARCHing foR LEgiSLATion
text: CCH IntelliConnect, Lexis Advance and Westlaw AU are also good places to search for journal articles referring to Australian legislation.
text_raw:
CCH IntelliConnect, Lexis Advance and Westlaw AU are also good places to 
search for journal articles referring to Australian legislation.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 19 SEARCHing foR LEgiSLATion
text: The journal collections on Lexis Advance and Westlaw AU are particularly extensive.
text_raw:
The journal collections on 
Lexis Advance and Westlaw AU are particularly extensive.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 19 SEARCHing foR LEgiSLATion
text: These three major online platforms also provide commentary services relevant to legislation, including some of the statute annotations services discussed at 19.26.
text_raw:
These three major online platforms also provide commentary services relevant to 
legislation, including some of the statute annotations services discussed at 19.26.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 19 SEARCHing foR LEgiSLATion
text: Other products provide summaries of legislation on specific topics, and updates on changes to legislation.
text_raw:
Other 
products provide summaries of legislation on specific topics, and updates on changes to 
legislation.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 19 SEARCHing foR LEgiSLATion
text: For example, each of the platforms contains extensive commentary concerning the Corporations Act 2001 (Cth) and related corporations legislation.
text_raw:
For example, each of the platforms contains extensive commentary concerning

chapter_title: CHAPTER 19 SEARCHing foR LEgiSLATion
text: Finding extrinsic materials Extrinsic materials are sources external to an Act, but closely related to it, that help to interpret the intention or meaning of that Act.
text_raw:
Finding extrinsic materials
Extrinsic materials are sources external to an Act, but closely related to it, that help to 
interpret the intention or meaning of that Act.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 19 SEARCHing foR LEgiSLATion
text: The use of extrinsic materials to aid statutory interpretation is explained in detail in Chapter 11.
text_raw:
The use of extrinsic materials to aid 
statutory interpretation is explained in detail in Chapter 11.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 19 SEARCHing foR LEgiSLATion
text: Section 15AB of the Acts Interpretation Act 1901 (Cth) (and equivalent legislation in some states and territories) lists the types of extrinsic materials that can be relied on to interpret an Act.
text_raw:
Section 15AB of the Acts Interpretation Act 1901 (Cth) (and equivalent legislation 
in some states and territories) lists the types of extrinsic materials that can be relied on 
to interpret an Act.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 19 SEARCHing foR LEgiSLATion
text: These include treaties or other international agreements referred to in an Act, and reports of law reform commissions, royal commissions or parliamentary committees.
text_raw:
These include treaties or other international agreements referred to 
in an Act, and reports of law reform commissions, royal commissions or parliamentary 
committees.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 19 SEARCHing foR LEgiSLATion
text: Extrinsic materials also include explanatory memoranda relating to a Bill (referred to in some jurisdictions as ‘explanatory notes’), the second reading speech of the Minister responsible for introducing a Bill and any official record of debates in Parliament.
text_raw:
Extrinsic materials also include explanatory memoranda relating to a Bill 
(referred to in some jurisdictions as ‘explanatory notes’), the second reading speech 
of the Minister responsible for introducing a Bill and any official record of debates in 
Parliament.

chapter_title: Chapter 22, which provides guidance on study skills, exam preparation and how to write
text: This chapter: • outlines different types of legal writing; • discusses how writing skills need to be developed and practised; • shows how effective writing uses appropriate structure, vocabulary and writing devices suited to the intended audience so as to achieve the intended purpose of the writing; • introduces specific principles of good legal writing, focusing on the plain language approach; • explains how proper referencing supports good writing; • covers the style conventions that you are expected to follow in legal writing; and • provides tips on writing legal essays.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: T o write effectively a writer must: • know what it is they are trying to achieve; • consider the intended readers of the document and whether the structure, vocabulary and tone they choose are appropriate for such an audience; and • take a plain language approach that is ‘clear, direct and straightforward’, enabling ‘readers to concentrate on the message conveyed, not on the difficulty of the language used’.8 WHAT iS THE WRiTER’S AiM?
text_raw:
T o write effectively a writer must: 
• know what it is they are trying to achieve; 
• consider the intended readers of the document and whether the structure, 
vocabulary and tone they choose are appropriate for such an audience; and 
• take a plain language approach that is ‘clear, direct and straightforward’, enabling 
‘readers to concentrate on the message conveyed, not on the difficulty of the 
language used’.8
WHAT iS THE WRiTER’S AiM?

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: Writing conventions In addition to the general and specific principles of good legal writing, there are also legal writing conventions that law students should seek to follow.
text_raw:
Writing conventions
In addition to the general and specific principles of good legal writing, there are also legal 
writing conventions that law students should seek to follow.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: These are only conventions, so not absolute.
text_raw:
These are only conventions, 
so not absolute.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: More specific requirements might be imposed for particular assignments, submissions for publication, or court or tribunal documents. ‘Style guides’, or lists of requirements about formatting, for example, are generally adopted by each law school or legal publication.
text_raw:
More specific requirements might be imposed for particular assignments, 
submissions for publication, or court or tribunal documents. ‘Style guides’, or lists of 
requirements about formatting, for example, are generally adopted by each law school or 
legal publication.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: The most commonly used guide for legal writing in Australia now is the Australian Guide to Legal Citation 24 (AGLC) which is used for Laying Down the Law and explained further in Chapter 21.
text_raw:
The most commonly used guide for legal writing in Australia now is the 
Australian Guide to Legal Citation 24 (AGLC) which is used for Laying Down the Law and

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: For any particular assignment or submission, students should find out which style guide has been adopted and seek to comply with it.
text_raw:

guide has been adopted and seek to comply with it.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: They should also check and seek to comply with requirements about formatting, submission and word limits.
text_raw:
They should also check and seek 
to comply with requirements about formatting, submission and word limits.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: Some law schools impose penalties for noncompliance with word limits, and courts often reject documents if they are not in the right format, so it is important to be informed and compliant.

text: LAYING DOWN THE LAW 558 FOOTnOTES, EnDnOTES, TABLES AnD BiBLiOgRAPHiES As a general rule, supporting references should be contained in notes.
text_raw:
LAYING DOWN THE LAW
558
FOOTnOTES, EnDnOTES, TABLES AnD BiBLiOgRAPHiES
As a general rule, supporting references should be contained in notes.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: These may be footnotes found at the bottom of each page, or endnotes found at the end of the work.
text_raw:
These may be 
footnotes found at the bottom of each page, or endnotes found at the end of the work.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: All notes begin with a capital letter and end with a full stop, and should be numbered consecutively.
text_raw:
All notes begin with a capital letter and end with a full stop, and should be numbered 
consecutively.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: As stated in 20.38–20.39, students must provide proper references for all statements of law and wherever they draw on the work of others, whether it is quoted or paraphrased.
text_raw:
As stated in 20.38–20.39, students must provide proper references for all statements 
of law and wherever they draw on the work of others, whether it is quoted or paraphrased.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: The precise way in which this is done, whether by way of footnotes, endnotes, tables or a bibliography, will depend upon the convention adopted by the institution to which the paper is being submitted.
text_raw:
The precise way in which this is done, whether by way of footnotes, endnotes, tables or 
a bibliography, will depend upon the convention adopted by the institution to which the 
paper is being submitted.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: The practice for exams differs, as noted in 22.32.
text_raw: The practice for exams differs, as noted in 22.32.

text: Citation of authority must comply with the applicable style guide, and the AGLC rules are summarised in Chapter 21.
text_raw:
Citation of authority must comply with the applicable style guide, and the AGLC 
rules are summarised in Chapter 21.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: If the reference is to a quotation, or to a discrete point, a ‘pinpoint reference’ is required, which is one that includes the specific page or paragraph where the quotation or point is located.
text_raw:
If the reference is to a quotation, or to a discrete 
point, a ‘pinpoint reference’ is required, which is one that includes the specific page or

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: Footnotes and endnotes may be used to make tangential points, but this is best done sparingly.
text_raw:
Footnotes and endnotes may be used 
to make tangential points, but this is best done sparingly.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: Footnotes and endnotes should not be used as a place to deposit content that does not fit into the body of an essay because of the need to conform to a prescribed word count; often limits on words in assignments will include such discursive footnotes.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: QUOTATiOnS Given the importance of precedent and authority in law, the use of quotations is common in legal writing.
text_raw:
QUOTATiOnS
Given the importance of precedent and authority in law, the use of quotations is common 
in legal writing.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: The extent to which quotations are used will depend on the particular form of legal writing.
text_raw:
The extent to which quotations are used will depend on the particular 
form of legal writing.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: If the object is to provide a comprehensive statement of law, as in a casebook or textbook, long quotations and case extracts may serve a useful purpose.
text_raw:
If the object is to provide a comprehensive statement of law, as in a 
casebook or textbook, long quotations and case extracts may serve a useful purpose.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: Parts of Laying Down the Law exemplify this: see, for example, case extracts in Chapter 7.
text_raw:
Parts 
of Laying Down the Law exemplify this: see, for example, case extracts in Chapter 7.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: If, however, an argument is being developed, quotations should be used only to the extent that they advance the argument.
text_raw:
If, 
however, an argument is being developed, quotations should be used only to the extent 
that they advance the argument.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: Sometimes the exact words of a quotation need to be provided, but often it will be more advantageous to paraphrase.
text_raw:
Sometimes the exact words of a quotation need to be 
provided, but often it will be more advantageous to paraphrase.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: Long quotations are rarely called for in legal argument.
text_raw:
Long quotations are rarely 
called for in legal argument.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: These comments apply both to arguments as to how current law applies to factual problems and more critical legal arguments.
text_raw:
These comments apply both to arguments as to how current 
law applies to factual problems and more critical legal arguments.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: Many students weaken their argument and receive lower marks in assignments because of the overuse of unnecessarily long quotations.
text_raw:
Many students weaken their argument and receive lower marks in assignments because 
of the overuse of unnecessarily long quotations.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: The ability of a student to paraphrase accurately has the added advantage of demonstrating the student’s understanding of the material.
text_raw:
The ability of a student to paraphrase 
accurately has the added advantage of demonstrating the student’s understanding of the 
material.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: Remember that even when another author’s ideas have been paraphrased rather than used word for word, they must be referenced.
text_raw:
Remember that even when another author’s ideas have been paraphrased rather 
than used word for word, they must be referenced.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: A quotation must be indicated as such by the use of single quotation marks.
text_raw: A quotation must be indicated as such by the use of single quotation marks.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: If, however, a quotation is more than three lines long, it is presented in block format: set apart, indented, with reduced font, and without quotation marks.25 If a quoted source contains a grammatical or typographical error, the Latin word ‘sic’ (‘so’ or ‘thus’) in square brackets can be included immediately after the error to show that something has been copied exactly from the original.
text_raw:
If, 
however, a quotation is more than three lines long, it is presented in block format: set 
apart, indented, with reduced font, and without quotation marks.25 
If a quoted source contains a grammatical or typographical error, the Latin word ‘sic’ 
(‘so’ or ‘thus’) in square brackets can be included immediately after the error to show that 
something has been copied exactly from the original.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: For example: ‘Some of the man [sic] detailed for the job were unavailable.’ 25 Ibid [1.5.1].

CAPiTALS

text: The general rule is that, unless the writer is referring to a specific institution, or to a specific holder of an office, the word should begin with a lower-case letter.
text_raw:

text: For example, generic words like court and government should always begin with a lower-case letter unless the author is referring to a specific court or government.

gRAMMAR AnD PUnCTUATiOn

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: Incorrect grammar or punctuation can significantly undermine the clarity of writing.
text_raw:
Incorrect grammar or punctuation can significantly 
undermine the clarity of writing.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: All writers should proofread their work carefully to identify and correct such errors.

All writers should proofread their work carefully to 
identify and correct such errors.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: Any writer who is not confident in their grasp of English grammar should pay attention to grammar-checking software or find and use reliable grammar resources.
text_raw:
Any writer who is not confident in their grasp of English 
grammar should pay attention to grammar-checking software or find and use reliable 
grammar resources.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: However, the rules of grammar do evolve and are arguably not as rigid as some pedants assert.
text_raw:
However, the rules of grammar do evolve and are arguably not as 
rigid as some pedants assert.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: Legal essay writing The two most common forms of assessment in law school are legal essays and problem responses that are akin to a legal advice.
text_raw:
Legal essay writing
The two most common forms of assessment in law school are legal essays and problem 
responses that are akin to a legal advice.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: Both are used to encourage and assess knowledge of the law, critical thinking and written communication.
text_raw:
Both are used to encourage and assess knowledge 
of the law, critical thinking and written communication.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: Problem responses require students to objectively determine what the law is in respect of a particular issue, apply the law to a specific set of given facts, and exercise judgement in suggesting a conclusion about how a court or tribunal would rule on the matter.
text_raw:
Problem responses require 
students to objectively determine what the law is in respect of a particular issue, apply 
the law to a specific set of given facts, and exercise judgement in suggesting a conclusion 
about how a court or tribunal would rule on the matter.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: (The role and requirements of problem responses are explained more fully at 20.10, 22.2 and 22.32.) In contrast, essay assessments are used to encourage students to research more widely, beyond the legal doctrine, and draw upon both primary and secondary sources of law.
text_raw:
(The role and requirements 
of problem responses are explained more fully at 20.10, 22.2 and 22.32.) In contrast, 
essay assessments are used to encourage students to research more widely, beyond the 
legal doctrine, and draw upon both primary and secondary sources of law.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: Essays require students to analyse the sources critically and, importantly, they call upon the student to synthesise the ideas and present the student’s own views to the reader in a balanced but persuasive way.
text_raw:
Essays require 
students to analyse the sources critically and, importantly, they call upon the student to 
synthesise the ideas and present the student’s own views to the reader in a balanced but 
persuasive way.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: CRiTiCAL THinKing Critical thinking is highly relevant to essay writing.
text_raw:
CRiTiCAL THinKing
Critical thinking is highly relevant to essay writing.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: Essay questions are often explicitly framed as a request for the student to ‘critically analyse’ an issue, legal response, case, proposal or theory.
text_raw:
Essay questions are often explicitly 
framed as a request for the student to ‘critically analyse’ an issue, legal response, case, 
proposal or theory.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: Even without this explicit reference, all essays require students to undertake critical thinking.
text_raw:
Even without this explicit reference, all essays require students to 
undertake critical thinking.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: As discussed in detail in 22.20–22.22, critical thinking means being able to reason objectively; underpinning this is the need to ask questions about facts, assertions, arguments and conclusions.
text_raw:
As discussed in detail in 22.20–22.22, critical thinking 
means being able to reason objectively; underpinning this is the need to ask questions 
about facts, assertions, arguments and conclusions.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: Critical thinking is required to enable students to develop their own informed opinion about a topic and express it in an essay.
text_raw:
Critical thinking is required to enable 
students to develop their own informed opinion about a topic and express it in an essay.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: Identifying and summarising the arguments of others can demonstrate good research and an understanding of a topic, but most assignments require more than a parroting of others.
text_raw:
Identifying and summarising the arguments of others can demonstrate good research 
and an understanding of a topic, but most assignments require more than a parroting of 
others.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: Usually in legal essay writing, students are expected to engage with the essay topic or question by providing arguments and counterarguments, based on research, as a means of developing their overall thesis or argument.
text_raw:
Usually in legal essay writing, students are expected to engage with the essay topic 
or question by providing arguments and counterarguments, based on research, as a means 
of developing their overall thesis or argument.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: This thesis should be derived from the student’s research, synthesis of sources and critical analysis.
text_raw:
This thesis should be derived from the 
student’s research, synthesis of sources and critical analysis.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: The thesis should drive an essay and be threaded throughout.
text_raw:
The thesis should drive an essay 
and be threaded throughout.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: Each argument or point within an essay should function to develop and strengthen the legitimacy of the student’s thesis.
text_raw:
Each argument or point within an essay should function 
to develop and strengthen the legitimacy of the student’s thesis.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: Counterarguments and flaws must be entertained rather than ignored; a thesis cannot simply be dogmatically asserted.
text_raw:
Counterarguments and 
flaws must be entertained rather than ignored; a thesis cannot simply be dogmatically 
asserted.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: If a counterargument can be refuted, this will strengthen the thesis.
text_raw: If a counterargument can be refuted, this will strengthen the thesis.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: Alternatively, the counterargument might express an alternative view or qualification to the conclusion.
text_raw:
Alternatively, 
the counterargument might express an alternative view or qualification to the conclusion.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: It is important that a legal essay should be persuasive, but at the same time remain balanced.
text_raw: It is important that a legal essay should be persuasive, but at the same time remain balanced.

text_raw:
561
Students in their early years of study are not expected to develop a wholly new 
argument or interpretation of the law in order to present a thesis or distinguish their ideas.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: However, critical thinking about sources must be demonstrated.
text_raw: However, critical thinking about sources must be demonstrated.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: Treating sources critically means asking the types of questions noted in 22.21.
text_raw:
Treating sources critically 
means asking the types of questions noted in 22.21.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: This will enable the students to engage with the ideas of others and explain whether they think they are justified.
text_raw:
This will enable the students to engage 
with the ideas of others and explain whether they think they are justified.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: Students must explain why they agree or disagree with ideas, arguments or interpretations, and justify that stance.
text_raw:
Students must 
explain why they agree or disagree with ideas, arguments or interpretations, and justify 
that stance.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: Later year students may extend or elaborate on the ideas or arguments of others.
text_raw:
Later year students may extend or elaborate on the ideas or arguments of 
others.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: This could be done by considering the appropriateness of the author’s apparent values, ideas of what the law aims to do, or the role of legal institutions or practitioners.
text_raw:
This could be done by considering the appropriateness of the author’s apparent 
values, ideas of what the law aims to do, or the role of legal institutions or practitioners.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: However, students must always keep in mind that their reasoning should be based primarily on research rather than what they think is correct.
text_raw:
However, students must always keep in mind that their reasoning should be based 
primarily on research rather than what they think is correct.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: Some students fall into the dangerous trap of manipulating or taking the ideas of others out of context in order to prop up their own thesis.
text_raw:
Some students fall into the 
dangerous trap of manipulating or taking the ideas of others out of context in order to 
prop up their own thesis.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: Students must be careful not to omit or dismiss research, simply because it does not accord with their own argument.
text_raw:
Students must be careful not to omit or dismiss research, simply 
because it does not accord with their own argument.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: Engaging in these practices is its own form of academic dishonesty.
text_raw:
Engaging in these practices is its 
own form of academic dishonesty.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: It is paramount that students do not misuse the sources upon which their legal essay is based.
text_raw:
It is paramount that students do not misuse the sources 
upon which their legal essay is based.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: In general, students should try to approach their research with an open mind, rather than a mind that is already decided on taking a certain path.
text_raw:
In general, students should try to approach their 
research with an open mind, rather than a mind that is already decided on taking a certain 
path.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: Often, students will have an argument in mind when they begin their research, and then in the course of the research realise they need to reconsider their position.
text_raw:

then in the course of the research realise they need to reconsider their position.

text: LAYING DOWN THE LAW 562 All legal essays should begin with an introduction, which leads the reader into the topic or subject matter, and tells the reader why the piece is being written.
text_raw:
LAYING DOWN THE LAW
562
All legal essays should begin with an introduction, which leads the reader into the 
topic or subject matter, and tells the reader why the piece is being written.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: Is it to provide an opinion on a particular legal problem?
text_raw:
Is it to provide 
an opinion on a particular legal problem?

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: Is it meant to be a balanced presentation of both sides of a case?
text_raw:
Is it meant to be a balanced presentation of both 
sides of a case?

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: Or is it intended to be partisan — to advance a certain line of argument?
text_raw: Or is it intended to be partisan — to advance a certain line of argument?

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: Does it provide a critical explanation of how the law operates?
text_raw: Does it provide a critical explanation of how the law operates?

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: Or does it argue for a change in the law?
text_raw:
Or does it argue for a 
change in the law?

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: In longer pieces of writing, the introduction should also foreshadow the major steps in the writer’s argument.
text_raw:
In longer pieces of writing, the introduction should also foreshadow 
the major steps in the writer’s argument.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: The scene should be set for the reader at the outset.
text_raw:
The scene should be set for the reader at the 
outset.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: Following the introduction, there should be a methodical presentation of the points to be made.
text_raw:
Following the introduction, there should be a methodical presentation of the points 
to be made.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: The use of separate headings often helps to organise the writer’s thoughts, and to identify for the reader the point or points to be focused on.
text_raw:
The use of separate headings often helps to organise the writer’s thoughts, 
and to identify for the reader the point or points to be focused on.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: If the author has more than one argument to make in support of a given point, it is generally best to begin with the strongest, and continue to the weakest.
text_raw:
If the author has more 
than one argument to make in support of a given point, it is generally best to begin with 
the strongest, and continue to the weakest.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: Some very good advocates employ a different method, saving their strongest arguments until last, but a writer should be confident before adopting that practice.
text_raw:
Some very good advocates employ a different 
method, saving their strongest arguments until last, but a writer should be confident 
before adopting that practice.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: As discussed at 20.48–20.49, essays require more than mere description.
text_raw: As discussed at 20.48–20.49, essays require more than mere description.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: They require critical analysis and argument, usually in response to a specific research question.
text_raw:
They 
require critical analysis and argument, usually in response to a specific research question.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: Some description of the law, context or relevant scholarship is always required, but this is only an intermediate step on the path to developing an argument.
text_raw:
Some description of the law, context or relevant scholarship is always required, but this is 
only an intermediate step on the path to developing an argument.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: Similarly, arguments need to be made, but if they are not supported with authority (as noted in 20.36–20.37), the job of writing is not complete.
text_raw:
Similarly, arguments 
need to be made, but if they are not supported with authority (as noted in 20.36–20.37), 
the job of writing is not complete.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: Finally, there should be a conclusion, summing up what has been said.
text_raw: Finally, there should be a conclusion, summing up what has been said.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: In effect, the conclusion’s aim is to provide a succinct ‘answer’ to the research question posed in the introduction.
text_raw:
In effect, the 
conclusion’s aim is to provide a succinct ‘answer’ to the research question posed in the 
introduction.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: Remember that while an essay should provide balanced and critical analysis of both sides or all angles on an issue, ultimately the writer is trying to persuade the reader of the validity of their conclusion.
text_raw:
Remember that while an essay should provide balanced and critical analysis 
of both sides or all angles on an issue, ultimately the writer is trying to persuade the reader 
of the validity of their conclusion.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: The conclusion should not be a re-hash of all that has been said, but it is one final opportunity to draw together the key points and lead the reader to the writer’s conclusion.
text_raw:
The conclusion should not be a re-hash of all that has 
been said, but it is one final opportunity to draw together the key points and lead the 
reader to the writer’s conclusion.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: One final tip: when timetabling your work, make sure that you leave adequate time for polishing and proofreading.
text_raw:
One final tip: when timetabling your work, make sure that you leave adequate 
time for polishing and proofreading.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: Before submission, read your answer carefully, sentence by sentence, one last time.
text_raw:
Before submission, read your answer carefully, 
sentence by sentence, one last time.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: As well as looking for typographical and grammatical errors, compliance with word limits and formatting requirements, check the writing for audience, aim and approach.
text_raw:
As well as looking for typographical and grammatical 
errors, compliance with word limits and formatting requirements, check the writing for 
audience, aim and approach.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: Consider what you are trying to achieve with the writing, keeping in mind who the audience is; ultimately, consider it for clarity.
text_raw:
Consider what you are trying to achieve with the writing, 
keeping in mind who the audience is; ultimately, consider it for clarity.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: In relation to each sentence and each paragraph, ask yourself whether it expresses precisely what you intend to say.
text_raw:
In relation to 
each sentence and each paragraph, ask yourself whether it expresses precisely what you 
intend to say.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: Is it clear and direct?
text_raw: Is it clear and direct?

text: Is the research question articulated in the introduction?
text_raw: Is the research question articulated in the introduction?

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: Has the essay done more than merely describe the law, facts or existing scholarship?
text_raw: Has the essay done more than merely describe the law, facts or existing scholarship?

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: Have arguments been supported with authority and have sources of authority been appropriately referenced?
text_raw:
Have arguments been supported with authority and have sources of authority been 
appropriately referenced?

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: Are there signposts such as headings, topic sentences and transitions to guide the reader through the argument?
text_raw:
Are there signposts such as headings, topic sentences and 
transitions to guide the reader through the argument?

text: Are there excessive or antiquated words, unnecessary jargon or convoluted constructions that need to be addressed?
text_raw:

words, unnecessary jargon or convoluted constructions that need to be addressed?

chapter_title: CHAPTER 20 LEgAL WRiTing
text: Finally, does the conclusion succinctly draw the arguments together, answering the question that is posed in the introduction?
text_raw:
Finally, 
does the conclusion succinctly draw the arguments together, answering the question that 
is posed in the introduction?

chapter_title: CHAPTER 21 REfEREnCing And CiTATion
text: 568 LAYING DOWN THE LAW Introduction When a writer needs to refer readers to other material, they provide a reference or citation to that other material.
text_raw:
568
LAYING DOWN THE LAW
Introduction
When a writer needs to refer readers to other material, they provide a reference or 
citation to that other material.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 21 REfEREnCing And CiTATion
text: This chapter outlines why, when and how such references should be provided in legal writing.
text_raw:
This chapter outlines why, when and how such references 
should be provided in legal writing.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 21 REfEREnCing And CiTATion
text: It focuses on: • the underlying rationales for referencing; • referencing conventions in legal citation; • how to determine when a reference to source material is needed, and how to refer to the same source again; and • style conventions for specific kinds of legal materials, including cases, statutes, books, journals and other sources commonly cited in legal writing.
text_raw:
It focuses on:
• the underlying rationales for referencing;
• referencing conventions in legal citation; 
• how to determine when a reference to source material is needed, and how to 
refer to the same source again; and 
• style conventions for specific kinds of legal materials, including cases, statutes, 
books, journals and other sources commonly cited in legal writing.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 21 REfEREnCing And CiTATion
text: The two main reasons a legal writer needs to reference other material are authority and honesty.
text_raw:
The two main reasons a legal writer needs to reference other material are authority 
and honesty.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 21 REfEREnCing And CiTATion
text: As discussed at 20.36–20.37, all assertions of what the law is should be supported by a reference to a primary source of law — legislation or case law — to support the assertion.
text_raw:
As discussed at 20.36–20.37, all assertions of what the law is should be 
supported by a reference to a primary source of law — legislation or case law — to 
support the assertion.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 21 REfEREnCing And CiTATion
text: Readers are then able to find that source for themselves to check the writer’s interpretation.
text_raw:
Readers are then able to find that source for themselves to check 
the writer’s interpretation.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 21 REfEREnCing And CiTATion
text: Other assertions — about facts or the views of others — should also be supported by reference to the source of that information.
text_raw:
Other assertions — about facts or the views of others — 
should also be supported by reference to the source of that information.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 21 REfEREnCing And CiTATion
text: This brings us to the second reason for referencing: whenever a writer uses an idea or words of another person, for the sake of honesty, they must declare this by referencing their source.
text_raw:
This brings us 
to the second reason for referencing: whenever a writer uses an idea or words of another 
person, for the sake of honesty, they must declare this by referencing their source.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 21 REfEREnCing And CiTATion
text: Failure to do so constitutes plagiarism, which is a type of academic dishonesty.
text_raw:
Failure 
to do so constitutes plagiarism, which is a type of academic dishonesty.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 21 REfEREnCing And CiTATion
text: (Writers might also provide references in footnotes to information and sources that are related to the author’s point but extraneous or secondary.) There are many rules about the content and format of references, but do not let this plethora of rules obscure the fundamental goals of referencing, which are to provide authority and to ensure honesty in your writing.
text_raw:
(Writers might 
also provide references in footnotes to information and sources that are related to the 
author’s point but extraneous or secondary.)
There are many rules about the content and format of references, but do not let 
this plethora of rules obscure the fundamental goals of referencing, which are to provide 
authority and to ensure honesty in your writing.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 21 REfEREnCing And CiTATion
text: Attention to referencing is an essential part of ensuring your own integrity as a writer and that your writing is effective.
text_raw:
Attention to referencing is an essential 
part of ensuring your own integrity as a writer and that your writing is effective.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 21 REfEREnCing And CiTATion
text: In this chapter we summarise key rules about the content and format of citations, drawn from the most commonly used legal citation style guide in Australia, the Australian Guide to Legal Citation (‘AGLC’).2 However, ‘[l]ike most things in life, legal citation and the application of the rules in the AGLC should be undertaken with a good measure of common sense.’3 If you keep in mind the purposes of providing a citation (authority and honesty), a few underlying principles emerge.
text_raw:
In this chapter we summarise key rules about the content and format of citations, 
drawn from the most commonly used legal citation style guide in Australia, the Australian 
Guide to Legal Citation (‘AGLC’).2 However, ‘[l]ike most things in life, legal citation and 
the application of the rules in the AGLC should be undertaken with a good measure of 
common sense.’3 If you keep in mind the purposes of providing a citation (authority and 
honesty), a few underlying principles emerge.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 21 REfEREnCing And CiTATion
text: Fundamentally the citation needs to be complete and correct.
text_raw:
Fundamentally the citation needs to be 
complete and correct.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 21 REfEREnCing And CiTATion
text: That is, it needs to provide enough information for the reader to be able to locate the source and, if necessary, a specific page or paragraph that supports the point, and this information obviously needs to be accurate.
text_raw:
That is, it needs to provide enough information for the reader to 
be able to locate the source and, if necessary, a specific page or paragraph that supports 
the point, and this information obviously needs to be accurate.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 21 REfEREnCing And CiTATion
text: Beyond that, the AGLC provides rules about how to provide the references, and these rules about formatting and content are designed to promote ‘clarity and consistency’.4 By agreeing on particular rules and applying them consistently, we can communicate substantial detail about sources clearly, precisely and succinctly.
text_raw:
Beyond that, the AGLC 
provides rules about how to provide the references, and these rules about formatting and 
content are designed to promote ‘clarity and consistency’.4 By agreeing on particular rules 
and applying them consistently, we can communicate substantial detail about sources 
clearly, precisely and succinctly.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 21 REfEREnCing And CiTATion
text: We work through the citation rules, looking at different types of authorities starting with primary sources, followed by various other secondary sources (books, articles and so on).

chapter_title: CHAPTER 21 REfEREnCing And CiTATion
text: Conventions in legal citation There is no single way to cite legal materials.
text_raw:
Conventions in legal citation
There is no single way to cite legal materials.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 21 REfEREnCing And CiTATion
text: Publishers have their own style guides which set out the citation rules for their publications (known as ‘house styles’).
text_raw:
Publishers have their own style guides which 
set out the citation rules for their publications (known as ‘house styles’).

chapter_title: CHAPTER 21 REfEREnCing And CiTATion
text: However, there are citation conventions that exist throughout common law jurisdictions.
text_raw:
However, there 
are citation conventions that exist throughout common law jurisdictions.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 21 REfEREnCing And CiTATion
text: The convention in legal writing is to use footnotes (or endnotes) to provide citations of sources, rather than ‘in text’ references.
text_raw:
The convention 
in legal writing is to use footnotes (or endnotes) to provide citations of sources, rather 
than ‘in text’ references.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 21 REfEREnCing And CiTATion
text: Students writing in other disciplines might use other styles, but need to abide by the legal referencing conventions for legal writing.
text_raw:
Students writing in other disciplines might use other styles, but 
need to abide by the legal referencing conventions for legal writing.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 21 REfEREnCing And CiTATion
text: For footnoting, the superscript footnote number should be inserted immediately after a clause or sentence that warrants support, not merely at the end of the paragraph.
text_raw:
For footnoting, the 
superscript footnote number should be inserted immediately after a clause or sentence 
that warrants support, not merely at the end of the paragraph.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 21 REfEREnCing And CiTATion
text: Y ou will see this convention followed throughout this book.
text_raw:
Y ou will see this convention 
followed throughout this book.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 21 REfEREnCing And CiTATion
text: One of the recent trends in Australian law and legal writing is a convergence in citation style.
text_raw:
One of the recent trends in Australian law and legal writing is a convergence in 
citation style.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 21 REfEREnCing And CiTATion
text: Differences in citation practices among Australian jurisdictions are no longer pronounced.
text_raw:
Differences in citation practices among Australian jurisdictions are no longer 
pronounced.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 21 REfEREnCing And CiTATion
text: In 1998 the Melbourne University Law Review Association contributed significantly to this convergence with the publication of the Australian Guide to Legal Citation.
text_raw:
In 1998 the Melbourne University Law Review Association contributed 
significantly to this convergence with the publication of the Australian Guide to Legal 
Citation.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 21 REfEREnCing And CiTATion
text: This guide has been adopted by a large and increasing number of Australian legal publications and was updated in 2002, 2010 and 2018.
text_raw:
This guide has been adopted by a large and increasing number of Australian legal 
publications and was updated in 2002, 2010 and 2018.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 21 REfEREnCing And CiTATion
text: Given the widespread use of AGLC, Laying Down the Law has adopted it for referencing.
text_raw:
Given the widespread use of AGLC, Laying Down the Law has adopted it for 
referencing.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 21 REfEREnCing And CiTATion
text: The advice on citation that is contained in this chapter is, therefore, consistent with the AGLC style.
text_raw:
The advice on citation that is contained in this chapter is, therefore, consistent 
with the AGLC style.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 21 REfEREnCing And CiTATion
text: However, whether the AGLC or another guide to citation is used, the writer should keep in mind the primary purposes of referencing — authority and honesty — and be guided by the principles of completeness and accuracy.
text_raw:
However, whether the AGLC or another guide to citation is used, 
the writer should keep in mind the primary purposes of referencing — authority and 
honesty — and be guided by the principles of completeness and accuracy.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 21 REfEREnCing And CiTATion
text: What sources should be referenced and when?
text_raw: What sources should be referenced and when?

chapter_title: CHAPTER 21 REfEREnCing And CiTATion
text: The dual purposes of authority and honesty can guide the reader in knowing when to provide a reference and what sources to reference.
text_raw:
The dual purposes of authority and honesty can guide the reader in knowing when to 
provide a reference and what sources to reference.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 21 REfEREnCing And CiTATion
text: An example is provided below, after the key principles are stated.
text_raw:
An example is provided below, after 
the key principles are stated.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 21 REfEREnCing And CiTATion
text: The first principle is that the best authority for a statement of the current law is the law itself, not commentary or someone else’s summary of it.
text_raw:
The first principle is that the best authority for a statement of the current law is 
the law itself, not commentary or someone else’s summary of it.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 21 REfEREnCing And CiTATion
text: This means providing a reference to legislation or case law, immediately after the statement of law.
text_raw:
This means providing a 
reference to legislation or case law, immediately after the statement of law.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 21 REfEREnCing And CiTATion
text: Of course, as a student, you may have relied on commentary about the law by experts and not been able to delve into all the primary sources.
text_raw:
Of course, as 
a student, you may have relied on commentary about the law by experts and not been 
able to delve into all the primary sources.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 21 REfEREnCing And CiTATion
text: In this case, it is important to keep in mind the honesty edict — the writer must disclose when they have used the views or words of another — and you should have honestly declared the secondary source in your reference.
text_raw:
In this case, it is important to keep in mind the 
honesty edict — the writer must disclose when they have used the views or words of 
another — and you should have honestly declared the secondary source in your reference.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 21 REfEREnCing And CiTATion
text: As an authority in law, a secondary source is not the best source and a court would not accept it as proof of the state of the law.
text_raw:
As an authority in law, a secondary source is not the best source and a court would not 
accept it as proof of the state of the law.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 21 REfEREnCing And CiTATion

chapter_title: CHAPTER 21 REfEREnCing And CiTATion
text: This does not include all facts; if something is well known and incontrovertible, it does not need a reference.
