text: From there an appeal may be made either to the County Court, to a single judge of the Supreme Court or, where appropriate, to the Federal Court.
text_raw:
From there an 
appeal may be made either to the County Court, to a single judge of the Supreme 
Court or, where appropriate, to the Federal Court.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: From the County Court and from a single judge of the Supreme Court, appeals go to the Court of Appeal.
text_raw:
From the County Court and from a 
single judge of the Supreme Court, appeals go to the Court of Appeal.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: Appeals also lie from the Court of Appeal and, in certain circumstances, a single judge of the Supreme Court to the High Court with the Court’s special leave.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: LAYING DOWN THE LAW 616 • The District Court is an intermediate court with extensive civil and criminal jurisdiction, some of which is appellate. • The Family Court of Western Australia exercises the jurisdiction exercised elsewhere in Australia by the national Family Court of Australia. • The Magistrates Court has a limited criminal and civil jurisdiction including in some family law matters. • The State Administrative Tribunal (SAT) has broad civil and administrative jurisdiction.
text_raw:
LAYING DOWN THE LAW
616
• The District Court is an intermediate court with extensive civil and criminal 
jurisdiction, some of which is appellate.
• The Family Court of Western Australia exercises the jurisdiction exercised 
elsewhere in Australia by the national Family Court of Australia.
• The Magistrates Court has a limited criminal and civil jurisdiction including in 
some family law matters.
• The State Administrative Tribunal (SAT) has broad civil and administrative 
jurisdiction.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: An appeal from the Magistrates Court in a civil matter can be made to the District Court, while appeal from the Magistrates Court in a criminal matter lies to a single judge of the Western Australian Supreme Court.
text_raw:
An appeal from the Magistrates Court in a civil matter can be made to the District 
Court, while appeal from the Magistrates Court in a criminal matter lies to a single 
judge of the Western Australian Supreme Court.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: From the District Court, the Family Court of Western Australia and a single judge of the Supreme Court, appeal lies to the Court of Appeal.
text_raw:
From the District Court, the Family 
Court of Western Australia and a single judge of the Supreme Court, appeal lies to 
the Court of Appeal.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: An appeal also lies to the Appeal Division of the Family Court of Australia from the Family Court of Western Australia.
text_raw:
An appeal also lies to the Appeal Division of the Family Court 
of Australia from the Family Court of Western Australia.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: From the Court of Appeal and, in certain circumstances, a single judge, appeal may be made to the High Court with the Court’s special leave.
text_raw:
From the Court of Appeal 
and, in certain circumstances, a single judge, appeal may be made to the High Court 
with the Court’s special leave.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: There is no right of internal review and appeals, by leave, go to the Supreme Court or the Court of Appeal.
text_raw:
There is no right of internal review and appeals, by leave, go to the Supreme Court 
or the Court of Appeal.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: Territory courts and tribunals Like Tasmania, the mainland Australian territories have only a two-tier court system, but like all states (soon including Tasmania), they also have tribunals.
text_raw:
Territory courts and tribunals
Like Tasmania, the mainland Australian territories have only a two-tier court system, but 
like all states (soon including Tasmania), they also have tribunals.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: The territories’ courts and tribunals are as follows. austraLiaN CaPitaL territor Y • The Supreme Court of the Australian Capital T erritory, usually presided over by a single judge, has general civil and criminal jurisdiction, both original and appellate.
text_raw:
The territories’ courts 
and tribunals are as follows.
austraLiaN CaPitaL territor Y

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: The Supreme Court is known as the Court of Appeal when exercising its appellate jurisdiction. • The Magistrates Court has a limited civil and criminal jurisdiction. • The ACT Civil and Administrative Tribunal (ACAT) has broad civil and administrative jurisdiction, original and appellate.
text_raw:
The Supreme Court is known as the Court of Appeal when exercising 
its appellate jurisdiction.
• The Magistrates Court has a limited civil and criminal jurisdiction.
• The ACT Civil and Administrative Tribunal (ACAT) has broad civil and 
administrative jurisdiction, original and appellate.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: There is a right of appeal from the Magistrates Court to the Supreme Court.
text_raw: There is a right of appeal from the Magistrates Court to the Supreme Court.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: Appeal from the Supreme Court is to the Full Court of the Federal Court and from there to the High Court with the Court’s special leave.
text_raw:
Appeal 
from the Supreme Court is to the Full Court of the Federal Court and from there to 
the High Court with the Court’s special leave.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: ACAT offers a right of internal review, as well as an appeal to the Supreme Court.
text_raw: ACAT offers a right of internal review, as well as an appeal to the Supreme Court.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: NortHerN territor Y • The Supreme Court of the Northern T erritory has general civil and criminal jurisdiction, original and appellate.
text_raw:
NortHerN territor Y
• The Supreme Court of the Northern T erritory has general civil and criminal 
jurisdiction, original and appellate.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: The Court is most frequently presided over by a single judge but also sits as a Court of Appeal, a Court of Criminal Appeal and, occasionally, as a Full Court.
text_raw:
The Court is most frequently presided over 
by a single judge but also sits as a Court of Appeal, a Court of Criminal Appeal

text: Court HierarCHies 617 • Local Court (formerly Magistrates Court) has civil and criminal jurisdiction (and members are referred to as judges, not magistrates). • The Northern T erritory Civil and Administrative Tribunal (NTCAT) has broad civil and administrative jurisdiction.
text_raw:
Court HierarCHies
617
• Local Court (formerly Magistrates Court) has civil and criminal jurisdiction 
(and members are referred to as judges, not magistrates).
• The Northern T erritory Civil and Administrative Tribunal (NTCAT) has broad 
civil and administrative jurisdiction.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: Appeals from the Local Court may be taken to the Supreme Court.
text_raw: Appeals from the Local Court may be taken to the Supreme Court.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: Appeals from a single judge of the Supreme Court usually lie to the Court of Appeal or the Court of Criminal Appeal, and then to the High Court with the Court’s special leave.
text_raw:
Appeals from a 
single judge of the Supreme Court usually lie to the Court of Appeal or the Court of 
Criminal Appeal, and then to the High Court with the Court’s special leave.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: There is a right of appeal from the NTCAT to an appeal panel of the Tribunal itself, and a right to appeal to the Supreme Court.
text_raw:
There is a right of appeal from the NTCAT to an appeal panel of the Tribunal itself, 
and a right to appeal to the Supreme Court.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: British courts and tribunals There is no single court system for the United Kingdom.
text_raw:
British courts and tribunals
There is no single court system for the United Kingdom.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: Separate court systems are in place for England and Wales, for Scotland, and for Northern Ireland.
text_raw:
Separate court systems are in 
place for England and Wales, for Scotland, and for Northern Ireland.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: Nonetheless, national jurisdiction exists for some areas, such as asylum and refugee claims, and military law. • The Supreme Court of the United Kingdom replaced the House of Lords in 2009 at the apex of the United Kingdom’s legal system.
text_raw:
Nonetheless, national 
jurisdiction exists for some areas, such as asylum and refugee claims, and military law.
• The Supreme Court of the United Kingdom replaced the House of Lords in 
2009 at the apex of the United Kingdom’s legal system.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: The Supreme Court hears appeals from courts in England and Wales, Scotland, and Northern Ireland.
text_raw:
The Supreme Court 
hears appeals from courts in England and Wales, Scotland, and Northern Ireland.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: Following are the main courts for the jurisdiction of England and Wales. • The Court of Appeal, as its name implies, is an appellate court with no original jurisdiction.
text_raw:
Following are the main courts for the jurisdiction of England and Wales. 
• The Court of Appeal, as its name implies, is an appellate court with no original 
jurisdiction.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: It is at the apex of the Senior Courts of England and Wales, which include the High Court and the Crown Court.
text_raw:
It is at the apex of the Senior Courts of England and Wales, which 
include the High Court and the Crown Court.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: The Court of Appeal has a Civil Division and a Criminal Division.
text_raw:
The Court of Appeal has a Civil 
Division and a Criminal Division.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: Appeals lie to the Supreme Court.
text_raw: Appeals lie to the Supreme Court.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: The Civil Division hears appeals from the courts below and from superior tribunals. • The High Court is composed of three Divisions: the Queen’s (or King’s) Bench Division, which includes the Commercial Court and the Admiralty Court; the Chancery Division; and the Family Division.
text_raw:
The Civil 
Division hears appeals from the courts below and from superior tribunals.
• The High Court is composed of three Divisions: the Queen’s (or King’s) Bench 
Division, which includes the Commercial Court and the Admiralty Court; 
the Chancery Division; and the Family Division.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: The jurisdiction of the High Court is mainly original but also, in part, appellate.
text_raw:
The jurisdiction of the High 
Court is mainly original but also, in part, appellate.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: Judges normally sit alone in the High Court but sometimes two or more sit together, thus forming a Divisional Court of the Queen’s Bench Division, the Family Division or the Chancery Division.
text_raw:
Judges normally sit alone 
in the High Court but sometimes two or more sit together, thus forming a 
Divisional Court of the Queen’s Bench Division, the Family Division or the 
Chancery Division.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: The Divisional Courts are intermediate appellate courts hearing appeals from inferior courts such as the Magistrates’ and County Courts, although they also have some original jurisdiction.
text_raw:
The Divisional Courts are intermediate appellate courts 
hearing appeals from inferior courts such as the Magistrates’ and County Courts, 
although they also have some original jurisdiction.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: The Divisional Court of the Queen’s Bench Division exercises supervisory jurisdiction over inferior courts, tribunals and other bodies, by way of prerogative writs. • The Crown Court is a criminal court with both original and appellate jurisdiction.
text_raw:
The Divisional Court of the 
Queen’s Bench Division exercises supervisory jurisdiction over inferior courts, 
tribunals and other bodies, by way of prerogative writs.
• The Crown Court is a criminal court with both original and appellate 
jurisdiction.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: When it sits as a court of first instance, trial may be by judge and jury, but when it hears appeals there is no jury.
text_raw:
When it sits as a court of first instance, trial may be by judge and 
jury, but when it hears appeals there is no jury.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: The Crown Court has a limited civil jurisdiction. • The County Courts are courts of limited original jurisdiction in a wide range of civil matters.
text_raw:
The Crown Court has a limited 
civil jurisdiction.
• The County Courts are courts of limited original jurisdiction in a wide range of 
civil matters.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: Actions are normally tried without a jury, although — for example, in a fraud case — a jury may be requested.
text_raw:
Actions are normally tried without a jury, although — for example, 
in a fraud case — a jury may be requested.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: LAYING DOWN THE LAW 618 • Magistrates’ courts are inferior courts with responsibility for some civil matters such as family proceedings and licensing, but their jurisdiction is mainly limited criminal jurisdiction.
text_raw:
LAYING DOWN THE LAW
618
• Magistrates’ courts are inferior courts with responsibility for some civil matters 
such as family proceedings and licensing, but their jurisdiction is mainly limited 
criminal jurisdiction.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: In civil proceedings, appeals are taken from magistrates’ courts or the County Courts to the Court of Appeal, one of the Divisional Courts or, occasionally, to a single High Court judge.
text_raw:
In civil proceedings, appeals are taken from magistrates’ courts or the County Courts 
to the Court of Appeal, one of the Divisional Courts or, occasionally, to a single High 
Court judge.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: Appeals from the High Court go to the Court of Appeal, Civil Division and then to the Supreme Court.
text_raw:
Appeals from the High Court go to the Court of Appeal, Civil Division 
and then to the Supreme Court.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: In certain circumstances appeals may be taken directly from the High Court to the Supreme Court.
text_raw:
In certain circumstances appeals may be taken directly 
from the High Court to the Supreme Court.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: The magistrates’ courts are at the lowest level of the criminal hierarchy.
text_raw: The magistrates’ courts are at the lowest level of the criminal hierarchy.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: More serious cases are tried in the Crown Court.
text_raw:
More serious 
cases are tried in the Crown Court.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: Appeals from the magistrates’ courts go to the Crown Court or the Divisional Court of the Queen’s Bench Division.
text_raw:
Appeals from the magistrates’ courts go to the Crown 
Court or the Divisional Court of the Queen’s Bench Division.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: Appeals from the Crown Court go to the Court of Appeal, Criminal Division and thence to the Supreme Court.
text_raw:
Appeals from the Crown 
Court go to the Court of Appeal, Criminal Division and thence to the Supreme Court.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: Appeals also lie from the Divisional Court to the Supreme Court.
text_raw: Appeals also lie from the Divisional Court to the Supreme Court.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: There are numerous specialist tribunals.
text_raw: There are numerous specialist tribunals.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: In 2008, the existing jurisdictions of many existing tribunals were combined in two new tribunals: the First-tier Tribunal (with divisions or chambers corresponding with the former tribunals); and an Upper Tribunal.
text_raw:
In 2008, the existing jurisdictions of many 
existing tribunals were combined in two new tribunals: the First-tier Tribunal (with 
divisions or chambers corresponding with the former tribunals); and an Upper Tribunal.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: The Upper Tribunal is a superior court of record, with equivalent status to the High Court.
text_raw:
The Upper Tribunal is a superior court of record, with equivalent status to the High 
Court.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: Legally qualified members of the Tribunals are judicial appointments.
text_raw: Legally qualified members of the Tribunals are judicial appointments.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: There is a right of appeal, on most matters with leave from the First-tier Tribunal to the Upper Tribunal, but the First-tier Tribunal may first reconsider its initial decision.
text_raw:
There is 
a right of appeal, on most matters with leave from the First-tier Tribunal to the Upper 
Tribunal, but the First-tier Tribunal may first reconsider its initial decision.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: First instance decisions on criminal injuries compensation and asylum support may be reviewed by the Upper Tribunal but only by way of judicial review.
text_raw:
First instance 
decisions on criminal injuries compensation and asylum support may be reviewed by the 
Upper Tribunal but only by way of judicial review.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: Appeals against decisions of the Upper Tribunal can be made to the Court of Appeal (in England and Wales) or the Court of Session (in Scotland).
text_raw:
Appeals against decisions of the Upper 
Tribunal can be made to the Court of Appeal (in England and Wales) or the Court of 
Session (in Scotland).

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: There is also an eponymous Employment Tribunal which has equivalent status to the Upper Tribunal and from which there is a similar right of appeal.
text_raw:
There is also an eponymous Employment Tribunal which has equivalent status to 
the Upper Tribunal and from which there is a similar right of appeal.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: With its exit from the European Union, unless the terms of the settlement later in 2020 decide otherwise, there will be no need for the United Kingdom to take matters to the Court of Justice of the European Union.
text_raw:
With its exit from the European Union, unless the terms of the settlement later in 2020 
decide otherwise, there will be no need for the United Kingdom to take matters to 
the Court of Justice of the European Union.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: Independently of the European Union, the United Kingdom is also a member of the European Convention on Human Rights 4 which are incorporated into British law by the Human Rights Act 1998 (UK).
text_raw:
Independently of the European Union, 
the United Kingdom is also a member of the European Convention on Human Rights 4 
which are incorporated into British law by the Human Rights Act 1998 (UK).

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: Persons who think that the British courts have not properly enforced their rights under the Convention may bring a case to the European Court of Human Rights in Strasbourg.
text_raw:
Persons 
who think that the British courts have not properly enforced their rights under the 
Convention may bring a case to the European Court of Human Rights in Strasbourg.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: There is ongoing debate as to whether the United Kingdom, having left the European Union, will also abandon the European Convention on Human Rights .
text_raw:
There is ongoing debate as to whether the United Kingdom, having left the European 
Union, will also abandon the European Convention on Human Rights .

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: Court HierarCHies 619 The main courts in the Canadian federal system, with judges federally appointed, are as follows: • The Supreme Court of Canada is the highest court in the Canadian hierarchy with both civil and criminal appellate jurisdiction.
text_raw:
Court HierarCHies
619
The main courts in the Canadian federal system, with judges federally appointed, 
are as follows:
• The Supreme Court of Canada is the highest court in the Canadian hierarchy 
with both civil and criminal appellate jurisdiction.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: It hears appeals from the Federal Court of Appeal, and other courts of appeal.
text_raw:
It hears appeals from the 
Federal Court of Appeal, and other courts of appeal.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: It also has the authority to deliver advisory opinions. • The Federal Court of Appeal hears appeals from the Federal Court (Trial Division) and from the Tax Court of Canada, and also adjudicates appeals under various federal Acts and from federal administrative tribunals. • The Court Martial Appeal Court hears appeals from military courts (courts martial). • The Tax Court of Canada has exclusive original jurisdiction to hear and determine appeals in respect of tax and welfare matters under specific Acts, including the Income T ax Act, RSC 1985; the Canada Pension Plan, RSC 1985; and the Employment Insurance Act, SC 1996.
text_raw:
It also has the authority to 
deliver advisory opinions.
• The Federal Court of Appeal hears appeals from the Federal Court (Trial 
Division) and from the Tax Court of Canada, and also adjudicates appeals under 
various federal Acts and from federal administrative tribunals.
• The Court Martial Appeal Court hears appeals from military courts (courts 
martial).
• The Tax Court of Canada has exclusive original jurisdiction to hear and 
determine appeals in respect of tax and welfare matters under specific Acts, 
including the Income T ax Act, RSC 1985; the Canada Pension Plan, RSC 1985; 
and the Employment Insurance Act, SC 1996.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: Canada also has a Canadian Human Rights Tribunal, established in 1977 under the Canadian Human Rights Act , RSC 1985.
text_raw:
Canada also has a Canadian Human Rights Tribunal, established in 1977 under 
the Canadian Human Rights Act , RSC  1985.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: There are a number of other federal administrative tribunals with jurisdiction over matters such as industrial relations, transportation, immigration and refugees, energy, and pensions.
text_raw:
There are a number of other federal 
administrative tribunals with jurisdiction over matters such as industrial relations, 
transportation, immigration and refugees, energy, and pensions.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: The Administrative Tribunals Support Service of Canada provides support services and facilities to 11 federal administrative tribunals by way of a single, integrated organisation.
text_raw:
The Administrative 
Tribunals Support Service of Canada provides support services and facilities to 
11 federal administrative tribunals by way of a single, integrated organisation.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: There is also a system of provincial and territory (lower) courts.
text_raw: There is also a system of provincial and territory (lower) courts.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: The general model is as follows: • Courts of superior jurisdiction of a province, or the Supreme Court of a province, have an Appellate Division, often referred to as the Court of Appeal of the province or territory, and a Trial Division, which in some provinces or territories is referred to as the Court of Queen’s Bench. • Provincial and T erritorial Courts have limited jurisdiction to try civil and criminal matters.
text_raw:
The general model 
is as follows:
• Courts of superior jurisdiction of a province, or the Supreme Court of a 
province, have an Appellate Division, often referred to as the Court of Appeal 
of the province or territory, and a Trial Division, which in some provinces or 
territories is referred to as the Court of Queen’s Bench.
• Provincial and T erritorial Courts have limited jurisdiction to try civil and 
criminal matters.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: In addition, the Canadian provinces have various specialist tribunals.
text_raw: In addition, the Canadian provinces have various specialist tribunals.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: In 1998 Quebec became the first province to introduce a general administrative tribunal (the Tribunal Administratif du Québec).
text_raw:
In 1998 Quebec 
became the first province to introduce a general administrative tribunal (the Tribunal 
Administratif du Québec).

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: In 2011, Ontario set up the Social Benefits Tribunal which administers a cluster of tribunals dealing with income support, human rights, landlord and tenant, child and family services, custody, and special education matters.
text_raw:
In 2011, Ontario set up the Social Benefits Tribunal which 
administers a cluster of tribunals dealing with income support, human rights, landlord 
and tenant, child and family services, custody, and special education matters.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: New Zealand courts and tribunals The New Zealand court hierarchy is as follows: • The Supreme Court of New Zealand is the ultimate appeal court for New Zealand. • The Court of Appeal hears and decides appeals from the High Court, the Employment Court, the Maori Appellate Court, the Courts Martial Appeal Court and other courts, and serious criminal charges on appeal from the District Court.
text_raw:
New Zealand courts and tribunals
The New Zealand court hierarchy is as follows:
• The Supreme Court of New Zealand is the ultimate appeal court for 
New Zealand.
• The Court of Appeal hears and decides appeals from the High Court, the 
Employment Court, the Maori Appellate Court, the Courts Martial Appeal 
Court and other courts, and serious criminal charges on appeal from the District 
Court.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: LAYING DOWN THE LAW 620 • The High Court hears and decides serious criminal charges as well as large or important civil cases and some appeals from the District Court.
text_raw:
LAYING DOWN THE LAW
620
• The High Court hears and decides serious criminal charges as well as large 
or important civil cases and some appeals from the District Court.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: It also has supervisory jurisdiction over tribunals. • The District Court has limited civil and criminal jurisdiction.
text_raw:
It also has 
supervisory jurisdiction over tribunals.
• The District Court has limited civil and criminal jurisdiction.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: It includes the Disputes Tribunal, Family Court and the Y outh Court.
text_raw:
It includes the 
Disputes Tribunal, Family Court and the Y outh Court.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: There is a range of specialist tribunals but, despite a recommendation by the law reform body in New Zealand, no general jurisdiction tribunal has yet been created.
text_raw:
There is a range of specialist tribunals but, despite a recommendation by the law reform 
body in New Zealand, no general jurisdiction tribunal has yet been created.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: US courts and tribunals The United States of America is a federation like Australia, and has a similar court hierarchy, but with a number of key differences.
text_raw:
US courts and tribunals
The United States of America is a federation like Australia, and has a similar court hierarchy, 
but with a number of key differences.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: First, the United States does not have a single or unitary court system: it has a federal system and 50 separate state systems.
text_raw:
First, the United States does not have a single or 
unitary court system: it has a federal system and 50 separate state systems.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: While the Supreme Court of the United States is considered the highest court of the land, its judgments are only precedential in respect of matters under federal jurisdiction and under the United States Constitution.
text_raw:
While the Supreme 
Court of the United States is considered the highest court of the land, its judgments are 
only precedential in respect of matters under federal jurisdiction and under the United 
States Constitution.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: The highest arbiter of any state’s law is the highest court in that state, not the US Supreme Court.
text_raw:
The highest arbiter of any state’s law is the highest court in that state, not 
the US Supreme Court.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: Each state has its own court hierarchy, usually with three levels from trial court, to immediate court, and ultimately the highest court which is a superior court often called a supreme court.
text_raw:
Each state has its own court hierarchy, usually with three levels 
from trial court, to immediate court, and ultimately the highest court which is a superior 
court often called a supreme court.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: Other than in respect of a matter relating to the United States Constitution (or federal law), appeals do not lie from state courts to federal courts.
text_raw:
Other than in respect of a matter relating to the United 
States Constitution (or federal law), appeals do not lie from state courts to federal courts.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: The second difference follows directly from the first: there is no single common law in the United States as the Supreme Court has no capacity to harmonise or reconcile different approaches on common law matters that develop in and across the states.
text_raw:
The second difference follows directly from the first: there is no single common 
law in the United States as the Supreme Court has no capacity to harmonise or reconcile 
different approaches on common law matters that develop in and across the states.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: This situation prompted establishment in 1923 of a private body, the American Law Institute (ALI), comprised of eminent legal academics, judges and other legal practitioners.
text_raw:
This 
situation prompted establishment in 1923 of a private body, the American Law Institute 
(ALI), comprised of eminent legal academics, judges and other legal practitioners.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: 5 The ALI has become a significant law reform body primarily through drafting ‘restatements’ in various common law fields.
text_raw:
5 The 
ALI has become a significant law reform body primarily through drafting ‘restatements’ 
in various common law fields.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: These documents summarise the state of the law across the nation in a particular field and provide guidance on the interpretation and reform of law.
text_raw:
These documents summarise the state of the law across 
the nation in a particular field and provide guidance on the interpretation and reform 
of law.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: In addition to restatements, the ALI has developed other law reform proposals as Principles of Law and even model codes in evidence and crime.
text_raw:
In addition to restatements, the ALI has developed other law reform proposals 
as Principles of Law and even model codes in evidence and crime.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: While not law, such restatements have significant persuasive authority.
text_raw:
While not law, such 
restatements have significant persuasive authority.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: The third difference relates to the structure of the federal court hierarchy, particularly the role of the intermediate courts.
text_raw:
The third difference relates to the structure of the federal court hierarchy, particularly 
the role of the intermediate courts.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: The federal court system has three tiers:
text_raw: The federal court system has three tiers:

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: District Courts (trial), Courts of Appeal (intermediate) and the Supreme Court.
text_raw:
District Courts 
(trial), Courts of Appeal (intermediate) and the Supreme Court.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: (There are also several courts of special jurisdiction.) The country is divided into 94 districts, providing the geographical jurisdiction for the District Courts, and these are arranged into 13 circuits with each circuit headed by a Court of Appeal.
text_raw:
(There are also several 
courts of special jurisdiction.) The country is divided into 94 districts, providing the 
geographical jurisdiction for the District Courts, and these are arranged into 13 circuits 
with each circuit headed by a Court of Appeal.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: Appeals from a District Court go to the relevant Circuit Court of Appeal and very few matters go beyond this level to the Supreme Court.
text_raw:
Appeals from a District Court go to 
the relevant Circuit Court of Appeal and very few matters go beyond this level to the 
Supreme Court.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: Each of the Circuit Courts of Appeal are not bound by the decisions of the other Courts of Appeal and thus, on any particular federal law matter, the law might be different across the circuits until the matter is heard and differences are reconciled by the Supreme Court.
text_raw:
Each of the Circuit Courts of Appeal are not bound by the decisions of 
the other Courts of Appeal and thus, on any particular federal law matter, the law might 
be different across the circuits until the matter is heard and differences are reconciled by 
the Supreme Court.

text: Australian report series This section sets out the most important series of court law reports in Australia. feDeraL The authorised series of reports are: • Commonwealth Law Reports (CLR), 1903–, contains decisions of the High Court and previously reported decisions of the Privy Council on appeal from Australian courts. • Federal Court Reports (FCR), 1984–, contains decisions of the Federal Court of Australia.
text_raw:
Australian report series
This section sets out the most important series of court law reports in Australia.
feDeraL
The authorised series of reports are:
• Commonwealth Law Reports (CLR), 1903–, contains decisions of the High 
Court and previously reported decisions of the Privy Council on appeal from 
Australian courts.
• Federal Court Reports (FCR), 1984–, contains decisions of the Federal Court of 
Australia.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: The main unauthorised series of reports include: • Australian Law Reports (ALR), 1973–, contains decisions of the High Court, state Supreme Courts exercising federal jurisdiction, and other federal courts and tribunals.
text_raw:
The main unauthorised series of reports include:
• Australian Law Reports (ALR), 1973–, contains decisions of the High Court, state 
Supreme Courts exercising federal jurisdiction, and other federal courts and 
tribunals.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: The Australian Law Reports series was preceded by the Australian Argus Law Reports (ALR), 1960–73, and the Argus Law Reports (ALR), 1895–1959.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: LAYING DOWN THE LAW 630 United States report series The main federal law reports in the United States include: • United States Reports (US), which contains the official reports of cases heard and decided in the United States Supreme Court. • Federal Reporter (F) and Federal Reporter, Second Series (F 2d) and Third Series (F 3d), although privately published (West), contain authorised reports of cases heard and decided in the United States Court of Appeals (the intermediate federal appellate court). • Federal Supplement (F Supp) contains official reports of cases heard and decided in the United States District Courts (the principal federal trial courts). • Federal Rules Decisions (FRD) contains full-text reports of cases heard and decided in the United States District Courts that are not otherwise designated for publication in the Federal Supplement and which involve matters raised under the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure and the Federal Rules of Criminal Procedure.
text_raw:
LAYING DOWN THE LAW
630
United States report series
The main federal law reports in the United States include:
• United States Reports (US), which contains the official reports of cases heard and 
decided in the United States Supreme Court.
• Federal Reporter (F) and Federal Reporter, Second Series (F  2d) and Third Series 
(F 3d), although privately published (West), contain authorised reports of cases 
heard and decided in the United States Court of Appeals (the intermediate 
federal appellate court).
• Federal Supplement (F Supp) contains official reports of cases heard and decided 
in the United States District Courts (the principal federal trial courts).
• Federal Rules Decisions (FRD) contains full-text reports of cases heard and 
decided in the United States District Courts that are not otherwise designated 
for publication in the Federal Supplement and which involve matters raised under 
the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure and the Federal Rules of Criminal Procedure.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: Important unauthorised series include: • Supreme Court Reporter (S Ct). • Lawyers’ Edition of the US Supreme Court Reports (L Ed and L Ed 2d). • United States Law Week (USLW) (looseleaf) provides the most current full-text publication of US Supreme Court decisions available in print.
text_raw:
Important unauthorised series include:
• Supreme Court Reporter (S Ct).
• Lawyers’ Edition of the US Supreme Court Reports (L Ed and L Ed 2d).
• United States Law Week (USLW) (looseleaf) provides the most current full-text 
publication of US Supreme Court decisions available in print.

chapter_title: CHAPTER 22 STudy And Ex Am SkillS
text: Other materials, including brief summaries of other major federal court decisions, are also contained in the series. • National Reporter Series (West) collects in regional volumes the decisions of all of the highest-level appellate courts in each of the states and most of their intermediate appellate courts.
